1.title: Science Fundamentals
1.description: Basic physics, chemistry, and biology concepts

chunks.content:
Physics is the study of matter and energy. Forces cause objects to move or change motion.

Newton's Three Laws of Motion:
1. First Law (Inertia): An object stays at rest or in motion unless acted on by a force.
   'Objects resist changes to their motion.'

2. Second Law: Force = Mass × Acceleration (F = ma)
   More mass → more force needed. More force → more acceleration.

3. Third Law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
   A rocket pushes gas backward; gas pushes rocket forward.

Types of Forces:
• Gravity: Pulls objects toward Earth (9.8 m/s²)
• Friction: Opposes motion between surfaces
• Normal Force: Perpendicular support from a surface
• Tension: Force through a string or rope

Chemistry studies matter and how it changes.

States of Matter:
• Solid: Fixed shape and volume, particles tightly packed
• Liquid: Fixed volume, takes shape of container, particles loosely packed
• Gas: No fixed shape or volume, particles spread far apart
• Plasma: Ionized gas at extreme temperatures

Atoms:
• The smallest unit of an element
• Made of: Protons (+), Neutrons (neutral), Electrons (-)
• Atomic Number = number of protons
• Mass Number = protons + neutrons

Elements and Compounds:
• Element: Pure substance made of one type of atom (H, O, Fe)
• Compound: Two or more elements chemically bonded (H₂O, CO₂)
• Mixture: Substances mixed but not bonded (saltwater)

chunks.topic: Cells — The Building Blocks of Life
chunks.content:
Biology studies living organisms. All life is made of cells.

Cell Theory:
1. All living things are made of cells
2. Cells are the basic unit of life
3. All cells come from pre-existing cells

Plant vs Animal Cells:
Animal Cell has: Nucleus, Mitochondria, Ribosomes, Cell membrane
Plant Cell additionally has: Cell wall, Chloroplasts, Large vacuole

Key Organelles:
• Nucleus: Control center, contains DNA
• Mitochondria: Produces energy (ATP) — 'powerhouse of the cell'
• Ribosome: Makes proteins
• Cell Membrane: Controls what enters/exits
• Chloroplast (plants): Converts sunlight to food (photosynthesis)

2.title: Intermediate Science
2.description: Waves, chemical reactions, genetics and ecosystems

chunks.content:
Waves transfer energy without transferring matter.

Wave Properties:
• Wavelength (λ): Distance between two peaks
• Frequency (f): Waves per second (Hz)
• Amplitude: Height of wave (related to energy)
• Wave Speed: v = f × λ

Types of Waves:
• Transverse: Particles move perpendicular to wave direction (light, water)
• Longitudinal: Particles move parallel to wave direction (sound)

Electromagnetic Spectrum (high to low frequency):
Gamma → X-ray → UV → Visible Light → Infrared → Microwave → Radio

Sound:
• Needs a medium (cannot travel in vacuum)
• Speed in air: ~343 m/s
• Pitch = frequency, Loudness = amplitude (decibels)

Chemical reactions break and form bonds, creating new substances.

Types of Reactions:
• Synthesis: A + B → AB (combining)
• Decomposition: AB → A + B (breaking apart)
• Combustion: Fuel + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + Energy
• Acid-Base: Acid + Base → Salt + Water

Balancing Equations:
H₂ + O₂ → H₂O becomes 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
(Law of Conservation of Mass: atoms can't be created or destroyed)

pH Scale:
• 0-6: Acidic (HCl, stomach acid)
• 7: Neutral (pure water)
• 8-14: Basic/Alkaline (baking soda, bleach)

Activation Energy: Minimum energy needed to start a reaction. Catalysts lower this.

Genetics studies heredity — how traits pass from parents to offspring.

DNA Structure:
• Double helix shape (Watson & Crick, 1953)
• Made of nucleotides: Sugar + Phosphate + Nitrogenous Base
• Bases: Adenine (A), Thymine (T), Guanine (G), Cytosine (C)
• A pairs with T, G pairs with C

From DNA to Protein:
DNA → (Transcription) → mRNA → (Translation) → Protein

Mendelian Genetics:
• Dominant allele (B) masks recessive (b)
• Genotype: Genetic makeup (BB, Bb, bb)
• Phenotype: Physical expression (Brown eyes, Blue eyes)
• Punnett Square predicts offspring probability

Humans: 46 chromosomes (23 pairs), 23 from each parent.

3.title: Advanced Science
3.description: Quantum physics, organic chemistry, and molecular biology

chunks.content:
Quantum mechanics describes physics at the atomic and subatomic scale.

Core Principles:
• Wave-Particle Duality: Light and matter behave as both waves and particles
• Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle: Cannot simultaneously know exact position AND momentum of a particle
• Quantization: Energy exists in discrete packets called quanta

Atomic Orbitals:
• Electrons occupy probability clouds, not fixed orbits
• Quantum Numbers: n (shell), l (shape), ml (orientation), ms (spin)
• Pauli Exclusion Principle: No two electrons can have the same four quantum numbers
• Aufbau Principle: Electrons fill lowest energy orbitals first

Schrodinger's Equation:
Describes how quantum states evolve over time. The solution gives a wavefunction (ψ) whose square gives the probability density of finding a particle.

Thermodynamics studies heat, energy, and their interconversion.

Laws of Thermodynamics:
0th Law: If A is in equilibrium with B, and B with C, then A is with C (temperature)
1st Law: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; ΔU = Q - W
2nd Law: Entropy (disorder) of the universe always increases
3rd Law: Entropy approaches zero as temperature approaches absolute zero

Key Concepts:
• Enthalpy (H): Heat content at constant pressure
• Entropy (S): Measure of disorder
• Gibbs Free Energy: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS
  • ΔG < 0: Spontaneous reaction
  • ΔG > 0: Non-spontaneous
  • ΔG = 0: Equilibrium

Carnot Efficiency: η = 1 - (T_cold/T_hot) — theoretical maximum efficiency of a heat engine.

Cellular respiration converts glucose to ATP energy.

Overall Equation:
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ATP

Three Stages:
1. Glycolysis (cytoplasm):
   Glucose (6C) → 2 Pyruvate (3C)
   Net gain: 2 ATP, 2 NADH

2. Krebs Cycle / Citric Acid Cycle (mitochondrial matrix):
   Pyruvate → Acetyl-CoA → CO₂ released
   Produces: 2 ATP, 8 NADH, 2 FADH₂ per glucose

3. Electron Transport Chain (inner mitochondrial membrane):
   NADH and FADH₂ donate electrons
   O₂ is final electron acceptor → H₂O formed
   Produces: ~32-34 ATP via chemiosmosis

Total yield: ~36-38 ATP per glucose molecule.
